title: Respiration in Humans
seo_title: Secondary 3 Biology: Respiration in Humans Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_text: Define aerobic and anaerobic respiration and state their word equations; describe the effect of lactic acid in muscles and the oxygen debt; identify the parts of the human gas exchange system and describe how the alveoli are adapted for gas exchange; describe the role of the intercostal muscles and diaphragm in breathing and the differences between inspired and expired air; describe the effects of nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide in tobacco smoke (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Biology worksheets on respiration in humans: aerobic and anaerobic respiration, oxygen debt, the lungs, alveoli, breathing, inspired and expired air, and smoking. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Respiration releases energy; breathing moves air.
key_sub: No oxygen: glucose → lactic acid, a small amount of energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Respiration happens in every cell; breathing happens in the lungs.

  • Aerobic: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + a lot of energy. Anaerobic (muscles): glucose → lactic acid + a little energy.
  • Air: nose → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Alveoli: large surface area, thin wall, moist, many capillaries.
  • Breathing in: external intercostals and diaphragm contract; thorax volume up, pressure down, air in.
  • Smoke: nicotine (addictive), tar (cancer, cilia), carbon monoxide (less oxygen carried).
Example

Need 4 dm³/min, get 3 dm³/min, 5 min. Oxygen debt?

(4 − 3) × 5

Answer: 5 dm³

Example

Diaphragm when breathing in?

contracts

flattens

Answer: contracts and flattens

Common mistakes

  • Calling breathing “respiration”.
  • Saying muscles make ethanol.
  • Saying the diaphragm relaxes when you breathe in.
  • Saying expired air contains no oxygen (it has about 16%).

faq.q: What is the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration?
faq.a: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and breaks glucose down completely to carbon dioxide and water, releasing a lot of energy. Anaerobic respiration in muscles uses no oxygen, makes lactic acid and releases much less energy.

faq.q: How are alveoli adapted for gas exchange?
faq.a: There are millions of them, giving a huge surface area; their walls are one cell thick; they are moist; and they are covered with capillaries that keep a steep concentration gradient.

faq.q: What happens when you breathe in?
faq.a: The external intercostal muscles contract, raising the ribs, and the diaphragm contracts and flattens. The volume of the thorax increases, the pressure falls and air rushes into the lungs.

items.q: During inspiration (breathing in), what happens to the internal intercostal muscles?
items.e: Breathing in: external intercostals and diaphragm contract, ribs up and out, thorax volume up, pressure down, air rushes in. Breathing out is the reverse.

items.e: Emphysema breaks down alveolar walls.

items.q: During 8 minutes of hard exercise a runner needs 5.0 dm³ of oxygen per minute, but can take in only 3.0 dm³ per minute. How large is the oxygen debt?
items.e: Oxygen debt = (5 − 3) × 8. It is repaid after exercise to break down lactic acid.
